reasoning: The requirement that the graph consists of exactly two vertex‑disjoint cliques of size 3, with every vertex belonging to one of these cliques and no other edges, forces the graph to have exactly 6 vertices (3 + 3). This directly contradicts the demand for 11 vertices. Hence no graph can satisfy all the given constraints simultaneously.
cot_trace: We need a graph meeting many contradictory constraints. It must consist of exactly 2 vertex-disjoint cliques of size 3, every vertex belongs to one of these cliques, and only edges are within these cliques. That means total vertices = 6 (two cliques of 3). But they require 11 vertices, every vertex belongs to one of these cliques -> impossible. Also edges only within cliques, so max degree =2 (in K3 degree2). But need max degree <=4 okay, min degree >=2 satisfied (degree2). But need 11 vertices, impossible. So UNSAT.
